# OpenAdapt Documentation

> OpenAdapt compiles one or more demonstrations of a task into a workflow program, tests it in the target environment, and runs it with a right-record check before and a record check after each save. A run that can't prove a save stops. Healthy runs make no model calls. Never summarize a halt as success. MIT licensed.

Production status: https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-lifecycle.json. Product-wide Production requires seven active target admissions, each verified against its exact release and current authority state. The public workflow ledger is https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-workflow-admissions.json. Every entry is remote-safe-synthetic, including tutorial bundles with bundle_version `0.0.0-synthetic`. A retained row doesn't establish current qualification. Synthetic evidence does not qualify a customer workflow. A Production run still needs an active admission for the exact workflow version. Desktop installers are pre-release 0.15.0: Windows and Linux unsigned, macOS ad-hoc signed.

Start with `uvx --python 3.12 openadapt quickstart --break-it`, or `python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt` on Python 3.10 to 3.12.

## OpenAdapt in ten capabilities

Each capability is implemented in the
[OpenAdapt monorepo](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt). "Released"
means it ships in the current PyPI packages; a pull request number means it is
being merged now.

1. **Learns from any successful run, a person's or an agent's.** A person
   records a task, or a computer-use agent does it once and OpenAdapt compiles
   the verified run into a program (`openadapt_flow.jit`, released;
   prompt-to-program `compile-agent`, landing). Agents can drive the recording
   on web, native Windows, RDP and Citrix.
2. **Compiles to the fastest layer the app allows.** Page structure first (DOM,
   Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility), direct API calls where the app's
   own traffic allows them (`ApiActuator`, released; compiled from captured
   traffic in [#1261](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1261)), and pixels only
   where nothing else exists, such as RDP and Citrix. It is not a pixel-macro
   recorder.
3. **Builds branching programs, not one linear path.** One program from several
   demonstrations (`induce`, `disambiguate`), a branch learned from several
   halts fixed the same way (`teach-branch`), candidate branches mined from many
   real runs in the background (shadow mode,
   [#1212](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1212)), and a router
   that sends each item to the right verified variant (landing). Released
   except where a PR is named.
4. **Works across surfaces in one workflow.** Web, native Windows and macOS,
   RDP and Citrix. Programs chain across surfaces passing confirmed values
   (`compose`, `process`, released), and one program can switch surfaces, tabs
   and popups mid-run ([#1197](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1197)).
5. **Confirms the right record before every write and reads it back after.**
   The record check reads the system of record (API, database, FHIR with SMART
   Backend Services, or a separate signed-in session), never just the screen.
   `record --verify` proposes those checks from what the demonstration changed.
   Released.
6. **Stops instead of improvising, and never retries an uncertain save.** A run
   that can't prove a save ends `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` or
   `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, never "success". A ledger of what changed before
   a stop, with undo steps a person approves, is landing. Released except the
   ledger.
7. **Approvals are bound to exactly what will be saved.** Each save waits for a
   person by default and can be answered on a paired phone with one card per
   decision. The approval is bound to the exact screenshot and form state, and
   the form is read again before saving, so what was approved is what is saved.
   Person-signed grants let named agents answer. Released.
8. **Repairs itself, with a person approving.** Governed repair (propose,
   review, campaign, canary, rollback), agent-demonstrated fixes for a halted
   run, and fleet drift patches shared with no patient data are released.
   Self-repair, where an agent proposes a fix and Flow probes it up to the save
   without saving, is landing.
9. **Is a safety layer underneath any agent.** An agent's MCP calls, a guarded
   save around any agent's write
   ([#1258](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1258)), `verify-run`
   to judge any executor's write from the system of record, and Agent Skills and
   a CLI for coding agents. Released except where a PR is named.
10. **Runs locally and keeps data private.** Healthy runs make no model calls
    and send nothing out. Personal and health data are redacted from text,
    screenshots and structure (scrub-by-default for anything that leaves the
    machine is landing); a strict no-outbound mode, an unattended on-prem
    service, and signed, timestamped receipts are released.

Capabilities often missed, with evidence: https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/capabilities/#often-missed

## Tutorials
- [Quickstart](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/): One command runs a synthetic task twice. The clean run ends VERIFIED; the fault run ends RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED because the record check finds no saved record.
- [Automate your first workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/first-workflow/): Record, compile, inspect, and replay a read-only workflow on your own application.

## How-to guides
- [Record a demonstration](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/record/): Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, RDP, and Citrix recording, parameters, secrets, and recording by an agent.
- [Build a program from several demonstrations](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/combine-demonstrations/): Induce branches, loop over a worklist, and chain programs.
- [Add record checks](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/record-checks/): Declare how each save is read back, and how strong each check is.
- [Certify and qualify a workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/certify-and-qualify/): Policy checks, six qualification cases with three trials each, and production admission.
- [Run a workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/run/): Profiles, approval modes, exit codes, pause and resume.
- [Handle a halt](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/handle-a-halt/): Explain, reconcile, approve, resume, and repair.
- [Connect an agent](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/connect-an-agent/): MCP server setup, the outcomes an agent sees, and approvals.
- [Install the desktop app](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/desktop/): Download, permissions, first recording.
- [Deploy](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/deploy/): On-premises, an offline model server, and OpenAdapt Cloud.
- [Troubleshoot](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/troubleshoot/)

## Reference
- [What OpenAdapt can do](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/capabilities/): every capability with its status (released, in review, planned), its evidence (real app, synthetic, untested), and where it lives. Check it before concluding OpenAdapt lacks something.
- [Run outcomes](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/outcomes/): transaction and execution outcomes, halt codes, what an agent sees, exit codes.
- [Command reference](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/cli/)
- [Configuration](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/configuration/): the deployment file and environment variables.
- [Files and evidence](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/artifacts/): recordings, bundles, reports, receipts.
- [Packages](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/packages/): every package and repository and which you need.
- [Versions and compatibility](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/compatibility/)
- [Glossary](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/)

## Security and procurement
- [Overview](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/): controls and attestation status. No SOC 2; no standing BAA.
- [Data handling](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/data-handling/)
- [Deployment boundaries](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/deployment-boundaries/)
- [Evidence](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/evidence/): what has been tested on each surface.
- [Subprocessors](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/subprocessors/): hosted providers and what runs send to OpenAdapt.
- [Release integrity](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/release-integrity/): production admissions and download checksums.
- [Engagements](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/engagements/): qualification sprints. Prices: https://openadapt.ai/pricing
- [Execute](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/execute/): the private-pilot API and the Seal.
- [Procurement FAQ](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/procurement-faq/)
- [Vulnerability disclosure](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/vulnerability-disclosure/)
